overview: A September 1939 Japanese telegraph-administration notice, routed via Bern and New York, warns that address-abbreviation restrictions produce undeliverable telegrams, citing regulations 71 and 93 and asking administrations to accept such messages only at sender's risk; two near-identical English copies survive, separated by a 'file not found' sheet.

people.name: J. C. R.
people.role: Unidentified person whose initials appear on the translation copy

subfiles.title: Telegram on insufficiently addressed messages to Japan
subfiles.from: Bern SCE Burinterna, transmitted through Cable Cable, New York
subfiles.about: The Japanese administration asks foreign telegraph administrations to exercise caution when accepting telegrams for Japan that lack adequate address information.
subfiles.summary: Notice reports telegrams to Japan often lack sufficient address detail partly due to abbreviation restrictions, citing regulations 71 and 93 and asking other administrations to accept such messages only at sender's risk.

subfiles.title: File not found notice
subfiles.about: An administrative notice records that a requested file could not be found.
subfiles.summary: Administrative slip simply reads 'FILE NOT FOUND' with the code 'CFIIV,' containing no substantive content.

subfiles.title: Translation of telegram on insufficient addresses
subfiles.from: Bern SCE Burinterna, transmitted through Cable Cable, New York
subfiles.about: This translation repeats the Japanese administration’s warning about telegrams for Japan that contain inadequate recipient addresses.
subfiles.summary: Translation repeats the notice that address-abbreviation restrictions produce undeliverable Japan-bound telegrams, citing regulations 71 and 93 and advising acceptance only at sender's risk.

interest: Shows a 1939 Japanese telegraph notice on insufficiently addressed mail, routed through Bern and New York to State.
